# altr

> AI enablement and automation firm in Tampa, Florida. We help growing teams use AI
> inside the work they already own, then automate the repeated parts. Founded by
> Alex Britton and Jarred Robidoux. In person across Tampa Bay, St. Petersburg and
> Clearwater; remote for teams anywhere in the United States. Focus: commercial real
> estate and operations-heavy teams, Claude enablement, MCP servers and agents.

Contact: inquiries@altrwork.com

## Engagements

- [Who we serve](https://altrwork.com/#who-we-serve): industry-specific service pages and three engagements in a fixed order, with no separate
 charge for the intro call. Fees are not published; they are quoted on a call and put in writing
 before anything is committed, because the right number depends on the team's size, location, and how
 far along they already are. Most engagements start with enablement, though a team that already knows where the work is can
 start at another service: hands-on work run against the
 team's own tools, in one of two formats, and a team can start with either. A working session is
 hands-on with the one to four people who own a process; it returns a written map of that workflow
 plus prompts built against real files. A team workshop covers up to ten people and is less hands-on
 with each person, producing no per-person map, but everyone leaves with something running. Neither
 is a prerequisite for the other. Session length is set with the client on the call and split however
 suits the team. Enablement output is prompts and workflows the team runs by
 hand. Agent build and deployment comes second, only if enablement finds something worth building,
 and is quoted as one fixed fee against written scope with hours named per workstream; the scope comes
 from the map enablement produced. A build means software engineering: multi-step agent orchestrations
 that act autonomously, MCP servers wiring agents into existing tools and permissions, deployed and
 monitored rather than run by hand. Consulting retainer is third: up to ten hours a month of advisory
 time, available only after an enablement engagement or a build, never as an entry point. Month to
 month or on a three or six month term, which costs less per month; unused hours roll one month.
 Retainer hours cover advisory work only. They are not a build slot, not engineering time,
 and not a workshop allowance; additional sessions, additional workshops, and
 anything needing real engineering are scoped and quoted separately. Model and infrastructure
 costs are billed by vendors directly to the client and are a small monthly amount at pilot volume.

## Services

- [AI consulting in Tampa](https://altrwork.com/ai-consulting-tampa.html): local service overview and common questions
- [Workflow automation consultant in Tampa](https://altrwork.com/workflow-automation-consultant-tampa.html): map one process, decide what to automate, then build automations and agents only when the path is clean
- [AI workflows for commercial real estate teams](https://altrwork.com/real-estate.html): the central CRE hub for brokerage, acquisitions, underwriting, asset and property operations, development diligence, connected systems, controlled file work, and recurring market monitoring
- [AI services for nonprofits](https://altrwork.com/nonprofits.html): program intake, funder research, workshops, reporting, and nonprofit operations
- [AI services for ecommerce](https://altrwork.com/ecommerce.html): product content, customer request triage, order operations, and repeatable production workflows
- [Strategy](https://altrwork.com/how-we-altr-work.html): the engagement itself, in three phases: map one repeated process, prove the value, then deploy
- [Workflow audit](https://altrwork.com/workflow-audit.html): the mapping phase on its own, before anything is built
- [Enablement](https://altrwork.com/ai-enablement-workshop.html): hands-on work against a team's own tasks, as a small-group working session or a full team workshop
- [Engineering](https://altrwork.com/custom-agents.html): workflow agents, agentic coding systems, automation handoff
- [Events](https://altrwork.com/ai-workshop.html): workshops, community demos, workflow reviews

## Case studies

- [Cloudflare Workers architecture](https://altrwork.com/impact-cloudflare-workers-architecture.html): two Workers, a service binding, two D1 databases, cron ingest, and a stateless MCP server
- [Automated invoicing on Stripe](https://altrwork.com/impact-automated-invoicing-stripe.html): one-command draft invoices, ACH ahead of card, and nightly reconciliation against Stripe
- [Tampa property records connector](https://altrwork.com/impact-cre-county-records-connector.html): Hillsborough, Pinellas, Pasco and Polk county records inside Claude, with branded valuations
- [Slice of Heaven Cakes](https://altrwork.com/impact-slice-of-heaven-cakes.html): website orders and quote requests into one pipeline with automatic confirmations and quoting
- [Contact](https://altrwork.com/contact.html): email, phone, and a free 30 minute call with altr in Tampa
- [Manhattan office condo registry](https://altrwork.com/impact-manhattan-office-condo-registry.html): every Manhattan office condominium assembled from ACRIS, the Digital Tax Map and the DOF assessment roll
- [spARK Labs, operations intake](https://altrwork.com/impact-spark-labs.html): expense and event request workflows in Claude Cowork
- [spARK Labs, remote MCP server](https://altrwork.com/impact-spark-labs-mcp.html): Cloudflare Workers MCP server connecting Claude to operations tools
- [spARK Labs, AIR Supply](https://altrwork.com/impact-spark-labs-air-supply.html): founder-advisor matching, shared records, monthly check-ins, and quarterly feedback
- [Fishin Prints](https://altrwork.com/impact-fishin-prints.html): catch photo to print-ready artwork workflow
- [BeBrief](https://altrwork.com/impact-bebrief.html): coding agents inside a full-stack build process

## Products

- [mortr](https://altrwork.com/mortr.html): CRM for commercial real estate teams with county property appraiser record lookup, contacts, a deal pipeline, and BOV generation in your firm’s branding. Property record coverage: Pinellas, Hillsborough, and Pasco counties, Florida. Uses dated public records. Book a demo through the contact page.

## Learning center

- [Learning center](https://altrwork.com/learn.html): every plain-answer page in one index, grouped as below

### What changed this month

- [AI news for business owners: September 2026](https://altrwork.com/ai-news-for-business-september-2026.html): Meta Muse, Instinct, custom GPTs retiring, Cowork merging into Claude, the new MCP spec, and what each means for a small team.

### Commercial real estate

- [How commercial real estate brokers use AI](https://altrwork.com/ai-for-commercial-real-estate-brokers.html): Prospecting from public record, BOVs, comps, CRM hygiene, and market updates, with what not to hand to a model.
- [MCP server for commercial real estate](https://altrwork.com/mcp-server-for-commercial-real-estate.html): What it does for a brokerage, what data can sit behind it, and the quiet failures to design against.
- [What is a broker opinion of value (BOV)?](https://altrwork.com/what-is-a-broker-opinion-of-value.html): What goes in one, how it differs from an appraisal, and what Florida law says it may not be called.
- [What Florida property appraiser data tells you](https://altrwork.com/florida-property-appraiser-data.html): Just value, DOR use codes, qualified sales, $100 deeds, portfolio sales, and what the roll never carries.
- [AI lease and rent roll abstraction](https://altrwork.com/ai-rent-roll-and-lease-abstraction.html): The fields to pull, how to check them, and where a person still has to read the lease.
- [AI in CRE underwriting: what it can and can't do](https://altrwork.com/ai-cre-underwriting.html): Normalizing T-12s and rent rolls, drafting memos, and why the value conclusion stays with the analyst.
- [AI tools for commercial real estate](https://altrwork.com/ai-tools-for-commercial-real-estate.html): A map by job to be done: assistants, data platforms, abstraction, underwriting, CRM, and public record.
- [Can Claude connect to CoStar?](https://altrwork.com/can-claude-connect-to-costar.html): There is no official connector, and CoStar's terms restrict AI access. What to automate instead.
- [Claude in CRE: Skills](https://altrwork.com/claude-cre-skills.html): Package the underwriting steps your team repeats into a playbook Claude follows.
- [Claude in CRE: Connectors](https://altrwork.com/claude-cre-connectors.html): Connect Claude to the CRM, property systems, and local market data.
- [Claude in CRE: Cowork](https://altrwork.com/claude-cre-cowork.html): Work directly inside approved local underwriting files.
- [Claude in CRE: Scheduled Tasks](https://altrwork.com/claude-cre-scheduled-tasks.html): Recurring market, pipeline, and property routines.

### Claude, MCP and agents

- [What is an MCP server?](https://altrwork.com/what-is-an-mcp-server.html): The Model Context Protocol for a business reader and a technical one: tools, resources, auth, and the security boundary.
- [What is an AI agent?](https://altrwork.com/what-is-an-ai-agent.html): Agent vs chatbot vs automation, the loop an agent runs, and where a person has to stay in it.
- [Personal AI agents like Meta Muse and Instinct](https://altrwork.com/personal-ai-agents-for-business.html): What consumer agents that act across your email, calendar and browser mean for a business, and the policy to set.
- [Claude Skills vs MCP](https://altrwork.com/claude-skills-vs-mcp.html): Skills package how Claude does a task. MCP is how it reaches a live system.
- [What is Claude Cowork?](https://altrwork.com/claude-cowork.html): Claude working inside an approved local folder so the deliverable stays on disk.
- [How to write a SKILL.md that gets used](https://altrwork.com/writing-a-skill-md.html): A sharp description, a lean body, and reference files loaded on demand.
- [MCP server design for internal AI tools](https://altrwork.com/mcp-server-design-internal-ai-tools.html): Tool boundaries, read vs write, schemas as contracts, approval and audit.
- [MCP agents and function calling](https://altrwork.com/mcp-agents-function-calling.html): Where tool-calling agents and MCP-connected workflows each fit.
- [LLM retrieval and grounded answers](https://altrwork.com/llm-retrieval-grounded-answers.html): Chunking, embedding, ranking, and keeping answers tied to sources.
- [RAG evaluation for internal knowledge bases](https://altrwork.com/rag-evaluation-internal-knowledge-bases.html): Measure retrieval quality and grounding before trusting it.
- [Context engineering for large codebases](https://altrwork.com/context-engineering-large-codebases.html): Repo instructions, retrieval, and definitions of done as infrastructure.
- [AI code review with judge agents](https://altrwork.com/ai-code-review-judge-agents.html): A judge-model loop that reviews pull requests without replacing the reviewer.

### Rolling AI out to a team

- [How to roll out Claude to a team](https://altrwork.com/how-to-roll-out-claude-to-a-team.html): One workflow first, then Projects, Skills, connectors, a data policy, and training.
- [AI training for employees: what sticks](https://altrwork.com/ai-training-for-employees.html): Train on the team's own tasks, not a feature tour, and measure what people keep using.
- [Claude prompts for small business owners](https://altrwork.com/claude-prompts-for-small-business.html): Copy-paste prompts from our free workshops, and how to turn a good one into a Skill.
- [AI governance for small and mid-size businesses](https://altrwork.com/ai-governance-lite-smb.html): A two-page AI policy, including a rule for personal AI agents like Meta Muse.
- [How to run an AI workflow audit yourself](https://altrwork.com/ai-workflow-audit-small-business.html): Map inputs, decisions, tools, outputs, and failure modes first.
- [The three phases of AI deployment](https://altrwork.com/three-phases-ai-deployment.html): Audit, pilot, controlled rollout.

### Buying AI services
